subject: Cloud Computing
title: Object Storage Explained
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Object Storage Explained.

hook.text: Amazon S3 stores over 350 trillion objects. It's the world's largest filing cabinet — by far.

buildup.text: Object storage treats each file as a flat object with metadata, not a folder in a hierarchy.

discovery.text: It's perfect for images, videos, backups, and logs — anything you write once and read many times.

twist.text: Object storage is cheap and durable. S3 promises 99.999999999% durability — eleven nines.

climax.text: Most data in the cloud lives in object storage. It's the default home for unstructured data.

punchline.text: Eleven nines of durability. Your data isn't going anywhere.

quiz.question: What makes object storage different from traditional file storage?
options: It stores files as flat objects with metadata instead of folder hierarchies
It can only store text files, not images or videos
It requires physical hard drives shipped to the data center

details.summary: Object storage like AWS S3 stores data as objects with metadata in flat namespaces, not hierarchical file systems. It offers virtually unlimited capacity, 99.999999999% durability, and scales effortlessly. Object storage is the primary storage model for cloud-native applications.
details.whyItMatters: Object storage is the default storage choice in the cloud because of its scalability, durability, and low cost. Understanding when to use it versus other storage types is a fundamental cloud skill.
takeaways: Objects are stored in flat namespaces with rich metadata
S3 offers 11 nines of durability across multiple facilities
Object storage scales to exabytes without management overhead

faq.question: What is the difference between object and file storage?
faq.answer: File storage uses hierarchical directories and supports file locking, making it suitable for shared access by applications. Object storage uses flat namespaces accessed via HTTP APIs, optimized for large-scale unstructured data like images, backups, and logs.

faq.question: How does S3 achieve such high durability?
faq.answer: S3 automatically replicates each object across multiple physically separated facilities within a region. It continuously verifies data integrity with checksums and automatically repairs any detected corruption. The 11 nines means you'd expect to lose one object per 10 million years.
